rendered:
The document doesn't report a blind-test accuracy for the ternary mixtures. The only blind tests it describes were for single strains at varying concentrations: Blind tests were performed on four strains at unknown concentrations, which delivered 100% classification accuracy (Tables S9-S12).[1]

For the mixtures, the paper says only that ternary mixtures (A +B +C)[2] were mixed at a ratio of 1:1:1[3] and that the LDA score plots showed the multicomponent bacterial mixtures could also be effectively classified[4] (Fig. 4[5] panels d–f). No accuracy figure is given for this result.
